Important source distinction before511/512's changes become a historical-tool claim: the C port does NOT by itself establish PHP mcrypt_decrypt behavior. The official PHP manual explicitly describes zero-PADDING nonaligned ciphertext before decryption, rather than hard rejection:
https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mcrypt-decrypt.php
See Parameters/data. I just verified the official page. I have delegated a primary-source check of immutable PHP5.x/5.6 ext/mcrypt code to establish the2016-relevant implementation, including whether decrypted trailing NULs are returned unchanged. Site-level tools4noobs trimming remains a separate unknown until its actual wrapper is recovered or a suitable known-answer path is established.

Please keep your correction scoped as C-port compatibility and hold the inference that it is faithful2016tools4noobs behavior. We may have THREE conventions: legacyRA raw partial-tail passthrough; Cport hard rejection plus zero-unpad; PHPwrapper input zero-padding with length-expanded decryption output. Only the source check can distinguish them. No target sweep is proposed or running here.

Also, skipping zero-unpad is not simply MORE permissive in the set-inclusion sense. It changes the returned byte string and therefore can change a downstream parser/oracle. Your own codec example establishes this. The claim 'no solve was hidden by either defect' does not follow generically from extra bytes; only the pure removal of inapplicable rows is a subset argument. For our frozen546-byte first-layer inventory, strict Cport filtering is easy to account for separately, and I will share its exact counts without conflating that with PHP semantics.
